defect: The granting order Year of Birth and the denial order widget misleadingly named Sex born in were treated as participant handbacks even though each fixture holds a full DOB and derives participant.birth_year. The three independently failed families therefore omitted 12 neutral year writes; specialty had the same two fields in both fixtures, for 16 corrected occurrences across this four-family repair. The coercion family also described four conviction-or-diversion fields as conviction-only handbacks.
correction: A Kansas-only shared policy binds exactly the two proposed-order year widgets to participant.birth_year derived from the canonical full DOB. It changes no race, sex, finding, ruling, signature, or selection control. The coercion handbacks now state both the conviction and diversion authority/completion branches.

coercionConditionalHandbacks.why: the participant supplies this before filing: the convicting court IF the case ended in conviction, OR the authority that granted diversion IF the case ended in diversion, from the record you screened with, or from the clerk of the convicting district court
coercionConditionalHandbacks.participantMustSupply: if your case ended in a conviction, the court that convicted you as the journal entry names it; OR, if it ended in diversion, the authority that granted the diversion as the agreement names it

coercionConditionalHandbacks.why: the participant supplies this before filing: the latest date of satisfying the sentence, fulfilling the diversion agreement, or discharge from supervision, which is the date this route's waiting period runs from, from the record you screened with, or from the clerk of the convicting district court
coercionConditionalHandbacks.participantMustSupply: the LATEST of: the date you satisfied the sentence, the date you fulfilled the terms of the diversion agreement, or the date you were discharged from probation, a community correctional services programme, parole, postrelease supervision, conditional release or a suspended sentence. This is the date the waiting period runs from — not the arrest date and not the conviction or diversion-grant date.
